title: OrgZoneBinding
description: Moss owner-local business intent + projection binding an organization to a Nexus zone. This is NOT a copy of Zone/ZoneGrant: external Zone/ZoneGrant/operation identities appear as opaque strings whose format is owned by their semantic owners (nexus-vfs zone-id projections, Nexus product contracts). Moss may cache display name/status observed from Nexus, but must mark observed revision/time and never treat this projection as authoritative Zone metadata.

api_version.description: iam family major. Unknown majors are rejected by this schema (const mismatch).

binding_id.description: Opaque binding identity; consumers do not parse its structure.

nexus_deployment_id.description: Identifies which Nexus deployment this binding targets.

zone_id.description: Opaque external Zone identity. Format rules are owned by nexus-vfs zone-id projections and are intentionally NOT re-validated here (no second truth).

purpose.description: Open string registry. Known values: default, office, core, shared. New purposes may be added within the same major.

desired_capabilities.description: Desired capability codes (open registry; e.g. zone.data.read).

resource_prefixes.description: Zone-internal absolute path prefixes. Canonicalization rules belong to the Nexus product contract; this schema only carries them.

sync_status.description: Projection of the observed Nexus-side state.

nexus_grant_id.description: Opaque external ZoneGrant identity once a grant exists.

nexus_operation_id.description: Opaque external ZoneOperation identity while a Nexus operation is in flight.

generation.description: Monotonic desired-state generation; reconciliation applies generations in order.

last_error_code.description: Open code registry; machine-readable, from the fixed/known error spaces this binding surfaces.

$comment: additionalProperties stays true on purpose: under a supported major, unknown optional fields are accepted at the wire layer and dropped when parsed into the object model (see the generated adapter). Setting it to false would turn unknown-optional into a rejection, which contradicts the family wire rules.
